title: Multi-Tenant Inference Decision Lab & Sell-Through Guide
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

Purpose: This pack is a compact, actionable sales enablement lab for conversations with platform and product engineering buyers evaluating multi-tenant inference. It bundles: positioning and a two-slide pitch narrative, a short competitive brief with rebuttals, three pricing scenarios (pilot → production → dedicated), two short case studies with measured outcomes, a security FAQ tailored to prospect concerns, and a 10-step implementation checklist. Use this during discovery calls, demo follow-ups, and pilot scoping workshops.

Audience: Platform engineers, ML infra leads, CTO/VP engineering, procurement (technical reviewers).

Executive pitch (2-slide narrative)

- Slide 1 - Problem & differentiator:
  - Most teams face unpredictable inference economics and brittle deployments when moving from prototype to production: latency spikes under burst, ballooning per-token costs, and complex rollouts across regions.
  - Redwood Inference provides a unified runtime and policy layer that optimizes latency, batching, and model variants across hosted, reserved, and private deployments. We reduce cost and operational risk while preserving developer velocity.

- Slide 2 - Outcomes we commit to (examples to cite):
  - Pilot goal: Validate 95th percentile gen latency ≤ 250 ms for short-turn prompts and design path to reduce per-token cost by ≥ 25% through batching + caching.
  - Production goal: Maintain 99.9% uptime across inference endpoints, predictable unit economics (cost-per-100k tokens), and a rollback policy that reduces model-regression blast radius.

Key differentiators & positioning statements

- Production-first developer experience: easy onboarding + transparent perf profiles for models (latency/throughput by sequence length).
- Unified runtime across hosting modes: same API, same observability, one rollout plan for hosted, dedicated, or private.
- Cost levers surfaced: batching/caching suggestions, quantization recommendations, and routing policies with measurable unit economics.
- Reliability primitives: automated fallbacks to compatible model variants and region-aware routing.

Competitive brief (short)

- Primary competitors in conversation: Managed cloud endpoints (major cloud providers), single-model-hosting vendors, and open-source self-hosted runtimes.
- Competitor strengths: broad cloud integrations, deep infra discounts, or DIY control.
- Redwood counterpoints:
  - Against cloud managed endpoints: We match/enhance developer UX while giving explicit cost controls (continuous batching, cache hit metrics) and predictable SLAs for committed customers.
  - Against single-vendor model hosts: We support model variety plus automated fallback to cheaper compatible model variants when capacity constraints or cost targets are triggered.
  - Against DIY runtimes: We offer a hardened runtime with workload-aware kernel selection, production observability, and rollback/rollout tools — removing months of ops work.

Common competitor objection & rebuttal examples:

1) Buyer: "We control cost by running on our cloud fleet."
   - Rebuttal: "We augment your fleet, or run in your VPC, but add automated batching, KV/prefix caching, and quantization profiles that typically reduce per-token spend 20–40% without accuracy loss. We can model expected savings during the pilot based on a 2-week sample trace."

2) Buyer: "We prefer open-source to avoid vendor lock-in."
   - Rebuttal: "Redwood supports deployment models that can be run in your VPC or on-prem, with model artifacts you can pin. Our offering focuses on the value around serving (routing, observability, safe rollouts) — not locking model weights."

Pricing guidance (scenarios & worked examples)

Notes: These scenarios should be presented as templates and adjusted for region, committed capacity, and model family. Always run the "pilot economics" worksheet with the prospect (sample dataset & token counts).

Table: Simplified pricing tiers (example numbers; use committed pricing tool during quoting)

| Tier         | Unit pricing example                    | Typical commitment | Typical use case |
|--------------|-----------------------------------------|--------------------|------------------|
| Pilot        | Hosted credits: $1,500 / month (includes 2M tokens and 50k embed units) | 1–3 months         | Validate latency & quality, measure token mix |
| Production   | $0.004 per 1k tokens gen (standard models), $0.01 per 1k tokens for large/LLM variants | month-to-month or monthly commit | Scale customer-facing features |
| Dedicated    | Reserved pool: $12k – $60k / month (depends on GPU class & throughput) + discounted per-token | 6–12 month commitment | Predictable throughput, enterprise isolation |

Worked pricing scenario (example):

- Prospect: marketplace app expecting 100M tokens/month (mixed gen + embeddings).
- Recommendation: Start pilot on hosted to validate prompt engineering and evals (2–4 weeks). If 95th latency targets met, move to Dedicated reserve with autoscale buffer for peak traffic. Expected uplift: 30% lower per-token cost vs unmanaged GPU fleet when batching and caching are enabled.

Pilot scoping playbook (4 steps)

1) Data intake & goals (Week 0): Collect example prompt set (5–20 prompts per feature), target latency SLO, and current monthly token estimate.
2) Sample trace (Week 1): Ingest 48–72 hours of traffic or synthetic trace. Run baseline with prospect infra metrics.
3) Optimization sprint (Week 2): Tune batching, enable prefix caching, evaluate quantization profile; produce cost/latency forecast.
4) Pilot review & next-step decision (Week 3–4): Present findings, propose Dedicated sizing or private deployment plan.

Case studies (two short vignettes)

1) DocuFlow — Legal automation SaaS
- Situation: DocuFlow needed faster document summarization in-product with predictable costs as usage scaled.
- Pilot: 3-week hosted pilot; Redwood ran a 48-hour trace and suggested batching + 8-bit quantization on the summarization model.
- Outcome: 95th percentile latency cut from 780 ms → 230 ms; monthly inference spend reduced by 37% as batching and KV caching removed duplicate prefix costs. Uptime improved to 99.95% after canary rollout.
- Selling points to highlight: measurable latency & cost wins, clear upgrade path to Dedicated for SLA-backed throughput.

2) ShopSmart — Personalization for mid-market commerce platform
- Situation: Latency-sensitive product recommendations and A/B model rollouts were causing increased ops overhead.
- Pilot: 4-week pilot including rollout policy and automated fallback to a smaller model variant during peak traffic.
- Outcome: 2x request throughput under same latency SLO; observed model-regression rollbacks reduced manual intervention by 85%. Estimated annualized cost savings vs unmanaged cluster: 28%.

Security & compliance FAQ (concise answers to common prospect questions)

Q: Where does customer data live?
A: For hosted customers data is stored in region-specific clusters (we support US, EU, APAC regions). For customers requiring isolation, we provide Dedicated or Private deployments in customer VPC/air-gapped on-prem.

Q: Do you support customer-managed KMS/HSM?
A: Yes. Private and Dedicated deployments integrate with customer KMS via KMIP or cloud provider KMS (IAM-bound). We also support HSM-backed key wraps for high-security use cases.

Q: Is there an audit trail for inference requests and model versions?
A: Yes. Audit logs capture request metadata, model version, route, and outcome codes. Logs can be shipped to customer SIEM (S3, CloudWatch, or customer syslog). Retention policies are configurable.

Q: How do you handle RBAC and least privilege?
A: Redwood Console supports role-based access with fine-grained permissions (route-level, model-level). Integrations: SSO (OIDC/SAML) and SCIM for provisioning.

Q: What certifications and security assessments are available?
A: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II readiness artifacts and runs quarterly external pentests. We provide an SSP and can complete customer questionnaires (e.g., SIG, CAIQ) under NDA.

Q: How do you prevent sensitive data from entering logs or becoming part of model training?
A: By default, hosted inference logs are metadata-only unless explicitly enabled. We do not use customer prompts to train shared models. Private deployments give customers control over data retention and telemetry.

Objection handling scripts (short)

- Objection: "We can't afford vendor migrations."
  - Script: "We treat portability as a first-class concern: model artifacts are your assets, API is consistent across hosting modes, and we include export/runbooks as part of the onboarding. Most customers see migration cost amortized quickly due to cost and ops savings."

- Objection: "Can you guarantee model quality if we quantize?"
  - Script: "We run quantization-aware evals on your prompt set during the pilot. Our Optimize toolkit recommends profiles that balance throughput with minimal quality impact, and we ship rollback policies if regressions are detected."

Implementation checklist (10-step, quick)

1) NDA and scoping signed; key contact and success criteria listed.
2) Provide sample prompt set and traffic trace (48–72 hours).
3) Configure pilot account and region; provide IP allowlist/VPC info if private.
4) Baseline run and collect metrics: p50/p95 latency, token mix, error types.
5) Apply initial batching/caching recommendations; enable detailed tracing.
6) Run quantization experiment (if appropriate) on dev branch; record eval metrics.
7) Establish rollout policy: canary % schedule, automatic rollback thresholds, and fallback model mapping.
8) Security review: KMS integration, retention, and SSO configuration.
9) Cost forecast review: present per-100k token estimates and committed pricing options.
10) Pilot close: hand-off to success for Dedicated sizing or Private deployment runbook.

Appendix: Example CLI snippets (for sales engineers to demo quickly)

- Generate (curl) sample:
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer <KEY>' \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"model":"redwood-alpha-1","input":"Summarize the following contract clause...","max_tokens":256}'

- Sample rollout policy (YAML excerpt):
  rollout_policy:
    - stage: canary
      percent: 5
      success_criteria:
        p95_latency_ms: 300
        error_rate_pct: 0.5
    - stage: gradual
      percent: 50
      duration: 2h
    - stage: all
      percent: 100

How to use this doc in the field

- Run the 4-step pilot scoping during discovery and attach the pricing worksheet.
- Use the executive 2-slide narrative at the start of any demo.
- Share the security FAQ proactively with infosec contacts; offer to run a dedicated technical review with our security architect.
